RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 25

The gender composition of a panel alone does not constitute evidence of bias; in education, panels frequently consist of women due to standard institutional staffing. Raising the panel's gender directly without concrete evidence will appear speculative and damage your professional credibility. 

Instead, send a polite follow-up regarding your requested written feedback. Focus your inquiry strictly on objective criteria: scoring rubrics, qualification weighting, and administrative experience relative to the job specification. If the written explanation reveals procedural irregularities, arbitrary scoring, or pretext, you can then consider consulting a union representative or legal counsel based on documented facts rather than demographic assumptions.
